reason: Founder checked: Bento Africa was led by founder and CEO Ebun Okubanjo, not Ope Akinyemi as the slate guessed. The episode cannot be told to the standard. Bento did not cleanly close: in early February 2025 its board 'temporarily' halted operations (TechCabal, 10 February 2025) after Okubanjo resigned on 30 January 2025 and the 10-person engineering team was laid off over unpaid January salaries. The halt is bound up with unresolved allegations that the company failed to remit clients' PAYE tax and pension deductions and forged tax receipts, under investigation by the Lagos State Internal Revenue Service and the EFCC (TechCabal 27 January 2025, Techpoint, Technext). Okubanjo denies wrongdoing; his only stated reason, in an email to investors, was that the business model did not work. No regulator finding, charge or court outcome could be found as of November 2026, and the company's final status is unclear. A story would have to centre on unadjudicated criminal allegations against a living person, which the brief's rule on attributing blame (only as courts, regulators or founders put it) does not allow. The other documented Bento episode, the board's 2022 suspension of Okubanjo after a toxic-workplace report (Nairametrics), is also allegation-based and unsuitable.
